issues.legal_issue: A High Court may revise an appellate decree that grants relief beyond the court’s authority in the suit.
material_facts: The suit sought possession, arrears of rent and mesne profits, while the tenant sought fixation of standard rent and dismissal of the suit.
The appellate court directed the landlord to render an account of overpaid rent, although it had no power to grant that relief in the suit.
issues.conclusion: The appellate court acted illegally and with material irregularity, so the High Court had jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure to revise its decree.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the High Court may revise a decree where the subordinate court has acted illegally or with material irregularity in exercising its jurisdiction. The appellate court had no power, on the pleadings in this suit, to direct an account of overpaid rent.

predicates.revision_from_appellate_decree: The matter is a revision from an appellate decree.
predicates.relief_beyond_suit_authority: The appellate court granted relief that it had no authority to grant in the suit.

issues.definition: When a revision challenges an appellate decree that grants relief beyond the court’s authority, the High Court may revise the decree.

issues.legal_issue: An overpayment of rent cannot be deducted from later rent after the right to recover that overpayment has become time-barred.
material_facts: The tenant paid rent in excess of the standard rent up to August 4, 1954.
The tenant did not deduct the overpayments from rent within six months of payment and instead later sued to recover them.
The tenant did not pay rent falling due after August 4, 1954.
issues.conclusion: The overpayments could not be deducted from or adjusted against rent falling due after August 4, 1954, and the rent was in arrears.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20 of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rents Control Act, 1947 gives a tenant six months from payment to recover overpaid rent, including by deduction from rent payable. Deduction is a mode of recovery and is subject to the same limitation as recovery by suit. The Court approved Sohrab Tavaria v. Jafferali, 58 Bom. L.R. 680, 687–88, and Karamsey Kanji v. Velji Virji, 56 Bom. L.R. 619, 626, and referred to Bayley v. Walker, [1925] 1 K.B. 447.

rule.if: tenant_rent_arrears_dispute and excess_rent_paid and overpayment_not_deducted_within_recovery_period and recovery_right_time_barred

predicates.tenant_rent_arrears_dispute: The case concerns a tenant’s alleged arrears of rent.
predicates.excess_rent_paid: The tenant paid more than the rent legally due.
predicates.overpayment_not_deducted_within_recovery: The tenant did not deduct the overpayment from rent while it remained recoverable.
predicates.recovery_right_time_barred: The tenant’s right to recover the overpayment had become time-barred.

issues.definition: If a tenant in a rent-arrears dispute paid excess rent but did not deduct it while recoverable, and the recovery right has become time-barred, that excess cannot offset later rent.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant in an eviction suit for rent default is not protected from eviction when the tenant is neither ready and willing to pay rent during the suit nor compliant with the required payment or deposit obligations.
material_facts: The tenant did not pay the standard rent falling due during the suit and claimed that no amount was payable.
The tenant did not pay or tender the standard rent at the first hearing or another date fixed by the trial court.
The tenant did not thereafter continue to pay or deposit rent in court until the suit was decided.
issues.conclusion: The tenant could not claim the protection of sections 12(1) or 12(3)(b) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rents Control Act, 1947, and the eviction decree was rightly granted.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 12(1) and 12(3)(b) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rents Control Act, 1947 require a tenant seeking protection in an eviction suit for rent default to be ready and willing to pay the standard rent during the suit and to pay or tender the rent due by the first hearing, thereafter continuing to pay or deposit it until the suit is decided.

rule.if: eviction_case_for_rent_default and not tenant_ready_and_willing_during_suit and not tenant_paid_or_tendered_by_first_hearing and not tenant_continued_payments_or_deposits

predicates.eviction_case_for_rent_default: The proceeding seeks eviction of a tenant for rent default.
predicates.tenant_ready_and_willing_during_suit: The tenant was ready and willing to pay the rent due while the suit was pending.
predicates.tenant_paid_or_tendered_by_first_hearing: The tenant paid or tendered the rent due by the first hearing or another date fixed by the court.
predicates.tenant_continued_payments_or_deposits: The tenant continued to pay or deposit rent until the suit was decided.

issues.definition: In an eviction case for rent default, a tenant who was not ready and willing to pay during the suit, did not pay or tender rent by the first hearing, and did not continue payments or deposits is not protected from eviction.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to the validity of a statutory rent-demand notice cannot be raised for the first time in revision when it was not raised in the courts below.
material_facts: At trial, the tenant disputed the validity of the notice to quit but did not challenge the validity of the statutory notice under section 12(2).
The tenant did not raise the statutory-notice challenge before the appellate court and first raised it in revision.
issues.conclusion: The High Court properly refused to allow the tenant to raise the statutory-notice challenge for the first time in revision, and the point was not open in the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: A ground not raised before the courts below may be refused when raised for the first time in revision. The Court applied this principle to the challenge concerning notice under section 12(2) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rents Control Act, 1947.

predicates.revision_proceeding: The proceeding is a revision before the High Court.
predicates.notice_validity_ground_not_raised_below: The party did not raise the notice-validity ground before the courts below.

issues.definition: In a revision proceeding, a notice-validity challenge that was not raised below may be refused.
